summary: Temporary masked access to production inference logs for Legal privacy review
description:
Issue summary:
Legal has requested a one-week access window to production inference logs to validate customer data handling claims for an upcoming compliance audit. Due to sensitivity, they require logs to be masked/obfuscated and access to be time-limited and fully audited.

Request details:
- Scope: Inference logs for customer 'Acme Health' (customer data referenced in application traces) from 2026-02-15 to 2026-03-08.
- Required fields: request_id, timestamp, route_id, model_version, input_prompt (masked), decoded tokens removed, output metadata, redaction_flags.
- Prohibitions: No raw PII or raw customer payloads; no unredacted training data identifiers.

Approvals required:
- Security approval (SRE/Infra): ensure masking pipeline and read-only access
- Compliance/Legal: confirm scope and retention
- Product/Data: confirm that requested fields suffice for audit

Audit expectations:
- Access recorded in central audit logs with KMS key ID
- Actions logged to Splunk/Datadog with user and session id
- Access TTL enforced via IAM token expiration
request_details: Legal requested masked prod logs dump (not full downloads) for evaluation. Preference for an S3 bucket with object-level SSE-KMS using key redwood-prod-logs-legal. Access must be via temporary IAM role assumed through Okta SAML and limited to group 'legal-audit'. Bucket objects should be pre-masked by the redwood masking lambda with documented mask algorithm.
steps_taken:
1) Initial triage by Support (Aisha) to verify scope and escalation path.
2) Eng on-call (Marco) reviewed masking feasibility and confirmed masking lambda exists but needs schema adjustment for new redaction_flags.
3) Security (Priya Patel) requested proof-of-concept of masking on a synthetic sample.
4) Generated masked sample and uploaded to pre-prod private bucket for Legal to preview.
investigation_notes:
Hypotheses:
- Existing masking pipeline covers common PII but not embedded base64/blobs present in some customer payloads.
- If uncovered, need to extend regex sanitizer and add decoding step for base64 detection.
Findings:
- Sample run found 2% of payloads with nested base64 strings; current sanitizer flagged them but did not decode for inner PII.
- No evidence of model training data exposure.
Links:
- Slack: #support (thread: 2026-03-10 legal-log-access)
- Confluence draft runbook: /confluence/redwood/runbooks/log-masking-procedure
- GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repos/infrastructure/pull/489
comments: Support (Aisha Khan) 2026-03-10: Raised by Legal during prep for client audit. Need to preserve minimal context for traceability while removing PII.
Oncall Eng (Marco Silva) 2026-03-11: Reviewed masking lambda. Can add base64 decode stage; estimate 1-2 engineering days to patch and validate in staging.
Security (Priya Patel) 2026-03-11: Require HMAC fingerprinting of original input to allow correlation without revealing content. Also require proofs of deletion after TTL.
Legal (Daniel Morris) 2026-03-11: Confirmed masked sample acceptable. Requested formal attestation that raw logs will not be accessible to Legal team at any point.
SRE (Liam O'Neill) 2026-03-12: Provisioned temporary bucket redwood-legal-audit-prod-2026-03 with SSE-KMS. IAM role redwood_legal_audit assumed via Okta; TTL set to 7 days. Audit logging enabled.
Support (Aisha Khan) 2026-03-12: Noted action items in ticket; awaiting sign-off from Compliance on masking POC and deletion attestation.
resolution: Provisioned time-limited, role-based read-only access to masked logs in S3 bucket redwood-legal-audit-prod-2026-03. Masking lambda updated to decode base64 segments and apply regex sanitizers. HMAC fingerprinting added to allow correlation without exposing raw content. KMS key redwood-prod-logs-legal used; access TTL 7 days enforced via IAM token expiry. Audit logs confirmed in Datadog and archived to compliance retention. Legal provided attestation of non-access to raw logs. Completed 2026-03-12.
follow_up_actions: Document masking algorithm and add unit tests (assigned to Eng Security)
Add automated pre-flight masking test to CI for any log-export pipeline changes
Update internal runbook with step-by-step checklist and approval form
Consider adding a self-service 'masked-log export' console action with built-in approvals
